Issues.Title: Don't fail the release when the Tailwind Play trigger fails
Issues.Body:
## Summary

"Trigger Tailwind Play update" ran as the last step of the `release` job, right after "Publish". When the trigger failed, the packages were already on npm, and the run went red. A re-run of the failed job ran "Publish" again, which npm rejected with E403 because that version was already published. So the run stayed red, and the trigger never ran.

Seen on `main`:

- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/42127576162: attempt 1 failed at the trigger (GitHub API error, `Unexpected end of JSON input`). Attempt 2 failed at "Publish".
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/36129580862: the same pattern on 2026-09-25, while `TAILWIND_PLAY_TOKEN` was SAML-protected. Runs 36128537256 and 36127696574 failed at the trigger too.

A failed Play update isn't worth a red release, so this PR stops it from failing the workflow, and still reports it:

- The trigger step stays in the `release` job, and has `continue-on-error: true`. On an error, it saves the error message as a step output, and a "Notify Discord about the Tailwind Play update" step posts it with a link to the run. The run also shows the error as an annotation.
- The Discord step continues on error too, so a failed Discord post can't fail the job after "Publish" either. It shows as an annotation on the run.
- No retry around the dispatch call.
- It still runs after each successful publish, for insiders and stable releases, as before.
- The `notify` job is unchanged.

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20749 also edits `release.yml`, in other places (the "Resolve release metadata" step and the `notify` label step), so the two should not conflict.

No changelog fragment: CI only.

## Test plan

This workflow runs only on `main` and on releases, so this PR can't run it.

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck off (`actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/release.yml`) reports no errors.
- With shellcheck on, it reports the same 15 `SC2086`/`SC2129` notes as `main`, all in `run:` scripts this PR does not touch.
- Read by hand: with step-level `continue-on-error`, a failed step has `outcome == 'failure'` and `conclusion == 'success'`, so the job and the run stay green, and the Discord step runs on `steps.trigger-play.outcome == 'failure'`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Don't fail the release when the Tailwind Play trigger fails" (#20750)

Issues.Title: Fix flaky integration tests and remove the global CI retry
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes the causes of the integration test flakes that the global CI retry (`retry: 2`) hid, and then removes that retry. [ci-all]

I looked at the integration jobs on `main` since 2026-08-25: 1736 jobs in 82 runs. In 72 of those runs, a retry saved at least one test. Each commit below fixes one cause. I confirmed each cause locally first, with a hook that makes the race happen every time. The old test fails with the hook and the new one passes.

| Commit | Test | First attempt failed | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 597d2bdc0 | upgrade: interrupted template migration | 69 of 82 Windows jobs | The hook let template writes finish 50ms after the truncation, and `taskkill` takes longer than that. |
| 4d1dda2a2 | CLI watch: source maps, removed dependency | 18 times, all 3 OSes | The tests read `out.css` while the CLI wrote it in place, or right after a `Done in` from an earlier event. |
| e2f838b6c | vite: external source file changes update the CSS | 21 of 80 macOS jobs | On macOS, chokidar starts the FSEvents stream only after a `stat` and a `realpath`, and gives no ready signal. A change before that is lost. |
| 070e9f8fa | postcss: rebuild error recovery | 2 of 82 Linux jobs | A late second build from step 2 read `tailwind.css` while step 3 rewrote it, and printed `Waiting for file changes...` for an empty file. |
| 9055d4185 | upgrade: interrupted template migration | | The hook now ends the process itself right after the truncation (`process.exit(42)`), so the test needs no timer, hanging promise or kill. |
| 0b26ae691 | all | | Remove the global retry. Keep `retry: 2` on CI only for the two Next.js tests that install from the npm registry. |

The commit messages have the details and the local reproductions.

## Not fixed, reported

- **Vite `watch mode` with lightningcss**: about 3 failures. Each one starts with a `dist/index.html 0.00 kB` build, and then no rebuild comes for 5s (for `index.css` on Linux, for `index.html` on Windows). I couldn't reproduce it on macOS, so I didn't guess at a fix. Without the retry, its next failure stays visible.
- **CLI ignored folder test**: 1 retry save, cause unknown.
- **Next.js tests in `postcss/next.test.ts`**: 4 saves. The failed attempts were slow or stuck installs from the npm registry, and the Next.js version even changed between attempts. That's outside our control, so these two tests keep a retry.
- **Nuxt dev mode** (6 failures) and **the bun half-upgrade test** (4 timeouts): a retry never saved them, so they fail the same with or without it.

## Follow-up

Some PostCSS tests still use a sleep (`postcss/source.test.ts`, `postcss/config.test.ts`) or an `expectFileNotToContain` without `await` (`postcss/source.test.ts`). They never flaked in this data, so I left them for a separate change.

## Test plan

- Each fixed test passes locally, also with the hook that reproduces its race. The old test fails with that hook.
- CI runs the full integration suite on all OSes (`[ci-all]`).

Issues.Title: Fix random Windows build crashes and invalid insiders versions
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes 2 causes of failing CI runs on `main`.

I looked at all jobs of the `CI` and `Integration Tests` runs for pushes to `main` from 2026-03-08 to 2026-11-23, and at the `Release` runs. Most failures have a cause outside this repo, like a slow npm registry or a failed Bun download. Two causes are bugs that we can fix here.

## Windows builds crash at random

About 1 in 100 Windows jobs fails in the `Build` step. That is about 1 in 12 pushes to `main`, as each push runs 9 Windows jobs. A re-run passes. The job fails in 1 of 2 ways:

- turbo exits with code 1 right after a task finishes, and prints nothing.
- The next task fails with `exited (-1073741502)`, which is `0xC0000142` (`STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED`). The post steps of the job fail in the same second.

The cause is a bug in turbo 2.9.15 up to 2.10.x. On Windows, after each task that exits with code 0, turbo kills every process whose recorded parent PID is the PID of the task. It does this after it released that PID, and it doesn't check when a process was created. Windows reuses PIDs, and it doesn't update the parent PID of a process whose parent exited. So turbo can kill processes that have nothing to do with the task, like turbo itself, or a process that new processes need to start.

https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/issues/13692 describes this bug. https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/pull/13695 fixed it, and the fix shipped in turbo 2.11.0.

The crashes started when we got turbo 2.9.18 on 2026-06-19, in https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20262:

| Period                   | turbo             | Windows jobs | `Build` crashes |
| ------------------------ | ----------------- | -----------: | --------------: |
| 2026-03-08 to 2026-06-18 | 2.7.6 to 2.9.14   |          900 |               0 |
| 2026-06-19 to 2026-11-23 | 2.9.18 and 2.10.8 |         1076 |              10 |

The crashes:

- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/29255625293/job/86835060989
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/29494150946/job/87607036034
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/30998298058/job/92280649474
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/36127696476/job/108047502713
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/38274004262/job/114894932348
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/38893967613/job/116949901324
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/42122838693/job/127579349944
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/43967446415/job/133650492514
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/44070236097/job/133994294317
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/45186508992/job/137733405719

The logs of the first 3 have expired, so I matched those by their annotations.

This PR upgrades turbo to 2.11.11. `turbo build --dry=json` gives the same 26 tasks, commands, dependencies and outputs as with 2.10.8.

## Some insiders releases fail to publish

The insiders version is `0.0.0-insiders.<short SHA>`. When the short SHA has only digits and starts with a zero, like `0607226`, it is a numeric pre-release identifier with a leading zero. Semver doesn't allow that, so `pnpm publish` fails with `EBADSEMVER`. A re-run fails the same way:

- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/44769705761 (`0.0.0-insiders.0607226`)
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/actions/runs/42834800232 (`0.0.0-insiders.0583144`)

The short SHA now always gets an `X` prefix. So `0607226` becomes `0.0.0-insiders.X0607226`, and each insiders version has the same form with an alphanumeric last identifier. The release job and the notify job both add it, so the Discord message names the published version.

## Test plan

- `semver.valid` rejects `0.0.0-insiders.0607226` and accepts `0.0.0-insiders.X0607226` and `0.0.0-insiders.Xabc1234`.
- `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run lint` pass locally with turbo 2.11.11.
- This PR has `[ci-all]`, so the Windows and macOS jobs run with turbo 2.11.11 too. One run can't prove that the crashes are gone, as they hit about 1 in 100 Windows jobs. The turbo source and the table above are the proof.

[ci-all]

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: don't collapse `leading-*` into the `text-*/*` modifier
Issues.Body:
## Summary

With `collapse: true`, canonicalization turned `text-sm leading-7` into `text-sm/7`. These are not equivalent:

- `text-sm` sets `line-height: var(--tw-leading, var(--text-sm--line-height))`.
- `leading-7` sets both `--tw-leading` and `line-height`.
- `text-sm/7` sets `line-height` directly, and doesn't set `--tw-leading`.

So `text-sm leading-7 md:text-base` collapsed into `text-sm/7 md:text-base`, and the line-height changed at `md`. The same goes for `hover:text-xs` and any other `text-*` in a variant on the same element. Descendants are not affected, because `--tw-leading` doesn't inherit.

Looking at the other classes in the list doesn't make this safe: the canonicalizer often sees only part of the classes of an element, like a `clsx`/`cva` fragment or a component prop.

The collapse came from `canonicalizeAst`, which ignored `--tw-leading` when `line-height` has the same value (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/19156, https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20593). This is the same bug class that https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20593 describes: a collapse drops a utility that sets a `--tw-*` variable. This PR removes `--tw-leading` from `TW_VARIABLE_PROPERTIES`. The other entries stay.

The pre-computed `text-{size}/{line-height}` utilities stay too, so arbitrary line-heights still collapse: `text-sm [line-height:28px]` → `text-sm/7`.

This replaces https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20603, which extended the collapse to `text-xs leading-none` → `text-xs/none`. Here, `text-xs leading-none` never collapses, also not after `text-xs/none` was canonicalized before. That removes the order dependence of the `leading-*` cases of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20602.

Part of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20602.

### Behavior changes

- `text-sm leading-7`, `text-xs leading-none`, `text-sm/6 leading-7`, … now stay as 2 classes. `leading-[28px]` still becomes `leading-7`.
- `[line-height:0]` → `leading-0` and `[line-height:1]` → `leading-none` no longer convert, because those utilities also set `--tw-leading`.
- The upgrade tool canonicalizes each candidate on its own, without `collapse`, so it never collapsed `text-*` and `leading-*`. But it's affected by the change above: `[line-height:theme(lineHeight.superLoose)]` now upgrades to `[line-height:var(--leading-superLoose)]` instead of `leading-superLoose`. The integration test expects that now. `[letter-spacing:…]` still becomes `tracking-*`.

### Not in this PR

`text-xs [line-height:1]` still depends on earlier calls: it stays as-is on a fresh design system, and becomes `text-xs/none` after `text-xs/none flex` was canonicalized. The pre-compute step only adds `text-{size}/{n}` for spacing multiples, so `text-{size}/none` only exists once something compiled it. That case doesn't involve `--tw-leading`, and it was the same before this PR.

## Test plan

- Updated the `font-size/line-height to text-{x}/{y}` tests: the `[line-height:*]` cases still collapse, the `leading-*` cases now stay. Added `text-xs leading-none`, `text-xs leading-[1.1]`, `text-xs leading-7 md:text-sm` and `text-xs leading-none hover:text-sm`.
- Added a regression test that `text-xs leading-none`, `text-sm leading-7`, … give the same result on a fresh design system and on one that already saw `text-xs/none`, `text-xs/[1.1]` and `text-sm/7`. It fails on `main`.
- The perf test from https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20558 expected `text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`. It now uses `w-10 h-10` → `size-10` as the collapse to check in the linked group. With the fix of that PR reverted locally, the test still runs out of memory.
- `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint`, `tsc`, all `tailwindcss` tests (5517), the `@tailwindcss/upgrade` tests (470) and the updated `upgrade/js-config.test.ts` integration test pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Canonicalization: don't collapse `leading-*` into the `text-*/*` modifier" (#20756)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: collapse static utilities regardless of earlier candidates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

part of #20602

collapsing static utilities like `overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-hidden` into `overflow-hidden` only worked after some earlier candidate built the pre-computed utilities since that is what indexes static utilities by property and value
collapse now builds them first so the result no longer depends on what was canonicalized before
the arbitrary line height cases from the issue comment are left out since they touch the same code as #20603

## Test plan

added a regression test that collapses `overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-hidden` and `overflow-x-clip overflow-y-clip` and `overscroll-x-none overscroll-y-none` on a new design system which fails on main and passes now
`pnpm vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` in packages/tailwindcss passes

Issues.Title: Remove duplicate tests and restore their intended inputs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

A few tests in `packages/tailwindcss` have the same body as a neighbouring test, so they ran the same check twice. Each pair went that way for a different reason:

- **`candidate.test.ts`: "implicit variable" tests.** These used to cover the automatic `var(…)` injection syntax (`bg-[--value]`). When that syntax was removed in #13657, their inputs were changed to `bg-[var(--value)]`, which is exactly what the "explicit variable" tests below them check. The implicit syntax is now the parens shorthand (`bg-(--value)`), so:
  - The non-important "implicit" tests are removed. `bg-(--my-color)` and `bg-red-500/(--value)` are already covered by `should parse a utility with an arbitrary value with parens` and `should parse a utility with an implicit variable as the modifier using the shorthand`.
  - The two `!important` "implicit" tests now use `bg-(--value)!` and `bg-red-500/(--value)!`. Those inputs had no coverage yet.
- **`css-functions.test.ts`: `theme("--color-red-500")`.** Its CSS has used the unquoted `theme(--color-red-500)` since it was added, so it repeated the test above it. It now uses the quoted form (`theme('--color-red-500')`), which nothing else tested. The title uses single quotes to match what Prettier writes in the CSS and the other quoted `theme('colors.red.500')` tests.
- **`replace-shadow-colors.test.ts`: `should handle box-shadow with intensity`.** When the `it.each` table was split into separate tests in #17435, the one `1px 1px var(--my-color)` intensity row became two identical tests. One of them is removed.

The duplicates were found with vitest-dedup (`duplicate-test` rule) and checked by hand against `git log`/`git blame`.

There are no source changes. No changelog entry, because this only touches tests.

## Test plan

```sh
# the three changed files: 1556 tests on main, 1553 with this change (the 3 removed duplicates)
cd packages/tailwindcss && pnpm vitest run src/candidate.test.ts src/css-functions.test.ts src/utils/replace-shadow-colors.test.ts

# whole tailwindcss package: 45 files, 5493 passed, 1 skipped
pnpm vitest run

# formatting of the changed files (from the repository root)
pnpm prettier --check packages/tailwindcss/src/candidate.test.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/css-functions.test.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/replace-shadow-colors.test.ts
```

To confirm the quoted `theme('--color-red-500')` test now covers unquoting, I disabled `eventuallyUnquote(path)` in `css-functions.ts`. That made this test fail while the unquoted one still passed. I then reverted the change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Remove duplicate tests and restore their intended inputs" (#20751)

Issues.Title: Release the roots of a finished build in `@tailwindcss/vite`
Issues.Body:
This PR makes `@tailwindcss/vite` release the compilers and scanners of a build once the build finishes.

On `main`, a finished build no longer keeps its plugin context or its module graph, thanks to https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20531 and https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20678. A probe like the one in the issue reports both as freed.

But the build plugin still keeps a `Root` for each CSS file of each environment, for as long as the plugin lives. Each root keeps its compiler, its scanner, and the resolvers of the environment that built it. So a process that keeps working after the build keeps all of them in memory. Examples are Astro, which renders its pages after the build, and Nuxt, which bundles the server with Nitro after the Vite builds. On Vite 8, Vite itself keeps the plugin alive after `build()`, so this happens even when the process drops the plugin.

This PR deletes the roots of an environment in `closeBundle`, except in watch mode, where rebuilds use them again. In watch mode, it deletes them in `closeWatcher`, once the watcher closes. Unlike the `rootsByEnv.clear()` that the issue suggests, it only deletes the roots of the environment that finished, so it doesn't touch environments that are still building. Dev mode doesn't change, because the hooks are on the build plugin only (`apply: 'build'`).

The hooks come from https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20503 by lazerg, who is a co-author of the commit.

## Behavior change

A reused builder (`builder.build(environment)` more than once) now starts each build of an environment with new roots. So it no longer generates CSS for classes that were removed since an earlier build, like a build in a new process. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20678 already starts the scans over in this case, but the roots kept their earlier candidates. The cost is that the second build sets up its compilers and scanners again.

## Memory

Heap after GC, while the process keeps the plugin, for a fixture with 2,000 modules and one Tailwind CSS root, on Node 24.22:

| | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vite 7, `build()` | 34.8 MiB | 23.4 MiB |
| Vite 7, builder with client and SSR | 46.6 MiB | 23.7 MiB |
| Vite 7, watch build after `close()` | 35.8 MiB | 23.0 MiB |
| Vite 8, `build()` | 33.8 MiB | 21.4 MiB |
| Vite 8, builder with client and SSR | 46.3 MiB | 22.5 MiB |

Before the build, the heap is 13.6 MiB with Vite 7 and 14.5 MiB with Vite 8. Each root keeps about 11 MiB here, so projects with more roots gain more. In a Nuxt project, https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20501#issuecomment-7003733555 measured about 130 MiB of live heap for the state of the plugin on `main`.

The fix also doesn't depend on how the runtime captures closures. On Bun 1.4, the heap of the builder goes from 59.3 MiB to 22.9 MiB.

What stays belongs to Vite. The plugin keeps the resolved `config` for its next build. On Vite 7, the config keeps the environment of the latest build, because `vite:prepare-out-dir` keeps a `Set` of the environments that it prepared. Vite 8 keeps its environments alive by itself.

## Test plan

- A new integration test checks that a finished build releases its compiler while the process keeps the plugin, and that a watch build keeps it until the watcher closes. A `@plugin` tracks an object that only the compiler keeps, with a `WeakRef`, and the scripts run with `node --expose-gc`.
- A new integration test checks that a reused builder doesn't keep a removed class.
- Both tests fail without the fix: the compiler stays alive, and `.font-bold` stays in the second build.
- Watch rebuilds still reuse their roots: with `DEBUG=tailwindcss`, the number of compiler setups doesn't change.
- `pnpm run build` and the Vite integration tests pass locally, except the tests whose `pnpm install` fails in my local setup (`?commonjs-proxy` and Nuxt).

Fixes https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20501

Issues.Title: fix: skip quoted strings in `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators`
Issues.Body:
## What

`addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` now skips over single- and double-quoted strings verbatim (honoring backslash escapes) instead of rewriting their contents.

## Why

Arbitrary values that contain a quoted string whose contents look like a math function call were being corrupted. For example:

```html
<div class="content-['(min(1,2))']">
```

was compiled to `content: "(min(1, 2))"` — the string literal's value was mutated because the parser treated the `min(1,2)` inside the quotes as a real math call and inserted spaces.

The function already tracks parentheses/brackets to avoid touching non-math values, but it had no notion of string literals, so any `(`, `)`, `,` or math operator inside quotes was misinterpreted.

## Fix

When the scanner encounters a `'` or `"`, it copies the entire string (until the matching unescaped quote) to the output unchanged and continues. Real math calls elsewhere in the same value are still formatted normally, e.g. `calc(1+2)_'(min(1,2))'` → `calc(1 + 2) '(min(1,2))'`.

## Testing

Added table-driven cases to `decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts` covering single/double quotes, escaped quotes, and a real math call adjacent to a quoted string.

```
pnpm --filter tailwindcss exec vitest run src/utils/decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts
✓ src/utils/decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts (82 tests) 189ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  82 passed (82)
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix: skip quoted strings in `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators`" (#20744)

Issues.Title: Always remove `tailwindcss/nesting` when migrating a PostCSS config
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Edit:** this PR now does more than the original fix below.
>
> Tailwind CSS v4 has no `tailwindcss/nesting` export. So a migrated PostCSS config that keeps the plugin fails to load with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Before, the upgrade removed `tailwindcss/nesting` only when it came right before `tailwindcss`. The lookahead for that case is what crashed on JSON configs where it was the last plugin.
>
> `@tailwindcss/postcss` handles nested CSS itself, so the upgrade now always removes `tailwindcss/nesting`, in both the JS and the JSON config path. This also removes the lookahead, and with it the crash.
>
> - The JSON integration test now expects `{ "@tailwindcss/postcss": {} }`.
> - A new JS integration test covers a plugin between `tailwindcss/nesting` and `tailwindcss`, which used to keep the plugin.
>
> <sub>Edit by an AI assistant on behalf of @RobinMalfait.</sub>

---

## Summary

`@tailwindcss/upgrade` crashes when `tailwindcss/nesting` is the last plugin in a JSON PostCSS config (`.postcssrc.json`, `.postcssrc` or the `postcss` key in `package.json`). For example:

```json
{ "plugins": { "tailwindcss": {}, "tailwindcss/nesting": {} } }
```

`migratePostCSSJsonConfig` destructures `plugins[i + 1]`, which is `undefined` for the last entry. The upgrade stops with `TypeError: undefined is not iterable`, exits 1 and leaves the PostCSS config unmigrated.

The fix checks that a next plugin exists before reading it. The plugin is then kept, the same way the JS config path already handles this case.

## Test plan

- Added an integration test in `integrations/upgrade/index.test.ts` with the config above. Without the fix it fails with the `TypeError`. With the fix it passes, and the config becomes `{ "@tailwindcss/postcss": {}, "tailwindcss/nesting": {} }`.
- `pnpm vitest --root=./integrations run upgrade/`: all tests pass.
- `pnpm vitest run`: all tests pass.
- `pnpm changelog check` and `prettier --check` pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Always remove `tailwindcss/nesting` when migrating a PostCSS config" (#20745)

Issues.Title: Fix `pnpm run lint` and re-enable the CI Lint step
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix `pnpm run lint` so it passes on `main`, and re-enable the CI Lint step.

Lint has not run in CI since 2024-10-08. Its `matrix.runner.os == 'ubuntu-latest'` condition did not match the Namespace runner. After the switch back to GitHub-hosted runners in https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20747, the step was disabled with `if: ${{ false }}` because it failed. This PR fixes those failures:

- **CI:** the Lint step runs again on the Linux runner. It now matches `matrix.runner.name == 'Linux'`, so a new runner label cannot turn it off again. **This changes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.**
- **`playgrounds/v3`:** remove the `next lint` script. Next 16 removed `next lint`, so Next read `lint` as a project directory and failed. The playground has no ESLint setup, and the `nextjs` playground has no lint script either.
- **Prettier:** ignore the generated WASI files in `crates/node` and `crates/node/npm/wasm32-wasi`. `crates/node/.gitignore` ignores them, but Prettier only reads the root `.gitignore`. This was the Linux failure in https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20747.
- **Package tsconfigs:** `include` in `packages/tsconfig.base.json` is read relative to `packages/`, so every package ran `tsc` over all packages with its own `lib` and types. That caused most of the errors, like `NodeList` not being iterable and missing Bun types. Each package now sets its own `include`. The `__tw_*` globals of the standalone CLI moved to a shared `packages/globals.d.ts` that the base config lists in `files`, since `@tailwindcss/node`, the CLI and the upgrade tool read them.
- **Type errors that then showed:**
  - `@tailwindcss/cli`: remove a `commands` field that `help()` never accepted (the output stays the same), and cast `new Console()`, which `bun-types` types too narrowly.
  - `@tailwindcss/standalone`: use `Bun.Build.CompileTarget`, as `Bun.Build.Target` no longer exists, and drop an unused `@ts-expect-error`.
  - `@tailwindcss/upgrade`: pass `src: undefined` to `resolveConfig()`, and add `es2023` to `lib` for `toSorted`.
  - `playgrounds/vite`: add DOM types.

This is CI and tooling only, so there is no changelog entry.

- `pnpm run lint`: Prettier is clean and all 7 lint tasks pass.
- `pnpm vitest run`: 6059 tests pass.

Issues.Title: group-has-* compiles to a :has() selector with a * subject, which makes Chromium restyle whole subtrees on every insertion
Issues.Body:
### What version of Tailwind CSS are you using? v4.3.3 ### What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using? @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 with Next.js ### What browser are you using? Chrome (Chromium 14x), measured with DevTools traces ### Describe your issue `group-has-*` compiles to a selector whose subject is `*`: ```css /* group-has-[[data-open]]:opacity-100 */ .group-has-\[\[data-open\]\]\:opacity-100:is(:where(.group):has([data-open]) *) { opacity: 1 } ``` Chromium keeps the `:has()` invalidation data per selector, and inside `:is(… *)` the descendant part has no class, id, tag or attribute to key on. So when any node is inserted or changes under any element that could be a `:has()` anchor, Chromium restyles the anchor's whole subtree instead of only the elements carrying the utility class. In our app, with about 50 `group-has-*` utilities in use, every DOM insertion paid for it: | Interaction (one inserted node) | Style recalc before | After the change below | | --- | --- | --- | | Append a `

` to a chat message, 1x CPU | 64.7 ms, 2,056 elements | 22.4 ms, 700 elements | | Same, 4x CPU throttle | 149.6 ms | 81.1 ms | | Insert a sent message, 1x / 4x | 62.8 / 161.3 ms | 34.1 / 94.4 ms | | Open a context menu, 1x / 4x | 93.6 / 314 ms | 55.8 / 198 ms | (UpdateLayoutTree p50 from a performance trace, production build. The remaining elements come from other rules.) The descendant form, which the `in-*` variant already uses, has the same meaning and the same specificity but keys on the utility's class: ```css :where(.group):has([data-open]) .group-has-\[\[data-open\]\]\:opacity-100 { opacity: 1 } ``` We patched the `group` compound variant to emit `${groupSelector} &` instead of `&:is(${groupSelector} *)` when the group selector contains `:has(`. We checked the change mechanically: all 52 changed rules have the same specificity, and `querySelectorAll` returned identical element sets for the old and new selector in 212 page states, including hover and focus. That fixed the cost above. The `peer-*` compound (`&:is(${sel} ~ *)`) has the same shape and would likely benefit too. We didn't measure it, because we don't use `peer-has-*`. Would you take a PR that emits the descendant form for `group-*` (at least when the group selector contains `:has()`)? Background on Chromium's `:has()` invalidation: https://blogs.igalia.com/blee/posts/2023/05/31/how-blink-invalidates-styles-when-has-in-use.html
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "group-has-* compiles to a :has() selector with a * subject, which makes Chromium restyle whole subtrees on every insertion" (#20741)

Issues.Title: Detect unbalanced outer braces in brace expansion
Issues.Body:
### Problem

In `packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/brace-expansion.ts`, `expand()` initializes `endIndex` to `rest.lastIndexOf('}')` before scanning for the matching closing brace at `depth === 0`:

```ts
let depth = 0
let endIndex = rest.lastIndexOf('}')
```

When an outer brace is unclosed while a nested brace is closed (e.g. `a{b,{c}`), the loop ends with `depth > 0` without finding a matching `}`, but `endIndex` retains the index of the inner `}` instead of `-1`. As a result, `expand()` misses the unbalanced outer group and recurses into the sliced inner content, throwing a truncated error (`The pattern \`{c\` is not balanced.`) instead of reporting the unbalanced pattern (`The pattern \`a{b,{c}\` is not balanced.`).

### Fix

- Initialize `endIndex = -1` (which also avoids an extra `lastIndexOf('}')` scan on every call) so `endIndex === -1` reliably detects when no matching closing brace exists.
- Add a regression test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/brace-expansion.test.ts`.

### Verification

- `.\node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/brace-expansion.test.ts` (22/22 passing; fails before fix)
- Prettier formatted and verified
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Detect unbalanced outer braces in brace expansion" (#20740)

Issues.Title: Return after circular dependency callback in topologicalSort
Issues.Body:
### Problem

In `packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/topological-sort.ts`, when a circular dependency is detected (`wip.has(node)`), `visit` invokes `options.onCircularDependency?.(path, node)` without returning:

```ts
if (wip.has(node)) options.onCircularDependency?.(path, node)
```

If `onCircularDependency` does not throw (for example, when collecting cycles or logging a warning), `visit` continues traversing the cycle and overflows the call stack (`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`).

### Fix

- Return immediately after calling `options.onCircularDependency?.(path, node)` when `wip.has(node)` is true.
- Add unit tests in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/topological-sort.test.ts`.

### Verification

- `.\node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/topological-sort.test.ts` (2/2 passing; fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before fix)
- `.\node_modules\.bin\prettier.cmd --check packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/topological-sort.ts packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/topological-sort.test.ts` (passing)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Return after circular dependency callback in topologicalSort" (#20739)

Issues.Title: Normalize case-insensitive CSS when we parse it
Issues.Body:
This PR lowercases the case-insensitive parts of CSS when we parse them, so the rest of the code can compare them as-is. It replaces one-off `toLowerCase()` calls and `/i` flags, and fixes the places that had no such check.

CSS is ASCII case-insensitive in many places: at-rule names, `!important`, function names, pseudo-class and pseudo-element names, units, CSS-wide keywords and URL schemes. We mostly compared them in lowercase only. On `main`:

```
@THEME { --color-brand: red; }         → printed as written, and `bg-brand` generates nothing
border-[2PX]                           → border-color: 2PX
@theme { --color-*: INITIAL; }         → Invalid theme value `INITIAL` for namespace `--color-*`
not-[@MEDIA_print]:flex                → generates nothing
.a { :IS(&) .b { … } }                 → .a :IS(&) .b
@import "HTTPS://example.com/a.css";   → passed to `loadStylesheet` like a local file
url(HTTPS://example.com/a.png)         → url(./foo/bar/HTTPS:/example.com/a.png) in an imported file
```

Each commit handles one layer, and its message has the details. So this PR is easiest to review commit by commit.

## Changes

- **At-rule names and `!important`**: `parseAtRule` lowercases the name, which also covers the at-rules of plugins and of `rule('@…')`. The AST of `@tailwindcss/postcss` skips our parser, so it lowercases the names itself. `!IMPORTANT` and `! important` are the `!important` flag now.
- **Function names**: the value parser lowercases them, e.g. `CALC(…)` becomes `calc(…)`. The 11 functions that CSS spells in camelCase get that spelling, e.g. `ROTATEX(…)` becomes `rotateX(…)`. Dashed functions, like `--spacing(…)`, are case-sensitive, so they stay as written. So do names that start with an escaped `-`, like `\--MY-FN(…)`. Raw arbitrary values get the same treatment before we validate them, so `bg-[URL(/a/*.png)]` is a `url(…)`.
- **Pseudo-class and pseudo-element names**: the selector parser lowercases them, and the `An+B` of `:nth-*(…)`. E.g. `:NTH-CHILD(2N+1 OF .Foo)` becomes `:nth-child(2n+1 of .Foo)`. Classes, IDs, attributes and the contents of functions like `:lang(EN)` stay as written.
- **Units**: the candidate parser lowercases units and exponents in arbitrary values, so `border-[2PX]` sets `border-width: 2px`. Strings, `url(…)`s, hashes and identifiers stay as written, and so does the value of a custom property.
- **CSS-wide keywords**: `INITIAL` becomes `initial` where values come in: the CSS parser, the AST of `@tailwindcss/postcss`, the theme of a JS config, and arbitrary values. This includes custom properties, because a CSS-wide keyword is always the whole value. The options of a `@plugin` are not CSS, so they stay as written.
- **Variants**: the at-rule name at the start of a variant selector is lowercase, so `not-[@MEDIA_print]:flex` and `@custom-variant print (@MEDIA print);` compound with `not-*`. Variant signatures print the parsed selector, so `[&:FOCUS]:flex` canonicalizes to `focus:flex`.
- **URL schemes**: `normalizeUrlScheme` lowercases only the scheme, because the rest of a URL can be case-sensitive. We use it in `@import`, in the `url(…)` rewriter of `@tailwindcss/node`, and in arbitrary values. A single letter is a Windows drive, like `C:`, so it stays as written.

These one-off checks are gone, because the parsers handle the case now:

- `toLowerCase()` for `url(…)` and `supports(…)` in `@import`.
- `toLowerCase()` for math functions in `hasMathFn` and `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators`.
- `toLowerCase()` for color and length functions in shadow values.
- `toLowerCase()` in `isPseudoElement` and `isStandardPseudoElement`.
- `toLowerCase()` for CSS-wide keywords in canonicalization.
- The `/i` flags of `IS_COLOR_FN` and `IS_LENGTH_FN`. With `/i`, `--ALPHA(…)` and `--SPACING(…)` counted as `--alpha(…)` and `--spacing(…)`, but dashed functions are case-sensitive.

## Output that changes on purpose

- User CSS prints at-rule names, CSS-wide keywords, `!important` and pseudo-classes in nested selectors in lowercase, e.g. `@MEDIA print` becomes `@media print`. The CSS does the same thing.
- `[&_:BEFORE]:flex` canonicalizes to `**:[&:before]:flex` instead of `**:[&:BEFORE]:flex`.
- `bg-[URL(_'image.png')]` is invalid now, like `bg-[url(_'image.png')]`.
- `text-[1q]` is a length now, like `text-[1Q]`.

## Out of scope

- Property names. We can't lowercase them when we parse, because `@plugin` options (like `className`), CSS Modules `:export` keys and `@font-feature-values` names are case-sensitive.
- Function names and URL schemes in plain CSS declarations, because the CSS parser doesn't parse values. E.g. `THEME(…)` doesn't resolve in CSS, but `w-[THEME(spacing.1)]` does.
- Media query params, e.g. `[@MEDIA_PRINT]:flex` becomes `[@media_PRINT]:flex`. `negateConditions` compares `not` in lowercase, but https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20664 rewrites it, so this PR leaves it alone.
- Arbitrary variants that don't match a named variant keep their case, e.g. `[&:HOVER]:flex`.
- Color keywords like `currentColor`, units in variant values and modifiers (`data-[size=10PX]` is a case-sensitive attribute value), the fallback of `--theme(--x, INITIAL)`, and the CSS-in-JS values of plugins.
- `URL(…)` in the `url(…)` rewriter of `@tailwindcss/node`: `cssUrlRE` only matches a lowercase `url(`, like Vite.

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20731 fixes the `@import` case with case-insensitive checks. This PR takes its tests, with its author as a co-author.

## Test plan

- Each commit adds tests next to the existing ones, e.g. in `css-parser.test.ts`, `value-parser.test.ts`, `selector-parser.test.ts`, `utilities.test.ts`, `variants.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`, `at-import.test.ts`, `urls.test.ts` and the tests of `@tailwindcss/postcss`.
- The new tests fail without the change of their commit.
- `pnpm vitest run` and `pnpm run build` pass.
- Benchmarks of bundled builds in Node, as the median of shuffled rounds, against `main` and a copy of `main` (A/A):
  - Parsing a 198 KiB stylesheet (the theme, Preflight and the CSS of about 2,400 candidates): 1.63 ms → 1.66 ms (+1.8%, A/A 0.0%).
  - A cold `compile` with the default theme, and a build of the 2,411 arbitrary candidates of this repo's tests: 19.63 ms → 19.73 ms (+0.5%, A/A -0.3%).
  - A cold `canonicalizeCandidates` call with 17 candidates with variants: 781 ms → 793 ms (+1.5%, A/A -0.7%).

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: don't unwrap `:is(…)` around a selector list in variant signatures
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes a bug where `canonicalizeCandidates` replaces an arbitrary variant with a custom variant that emits different CSS.

`createVariantSignatureCache` replaces `:is(…)` with its child when it has a single child. That child can be a selector list. Then `&:is(.foo,.bar)` becomes `&.foo,.bar`. In nesting, that means `&.foo, & .bar`, so `.bar` turns into a descendant.

```css
@custom-variant foo (&.foo, .bar);
```

Before this PR, `[&:is(.foo,.bar)]:flex` canonicalized to `foo:flex`, but the two emit different CSS:

```css
.foo\:flex.foo, .foo\:flex .bar { display: flex; }
.\[\&\:is\(\.foo\,\.bar\)\]\:flex:is(.foo, .bar) { display: flex; }
```

`[&:is(.foo,_.bar)]:flex` and `[&_:is(.foo,.bar)]:flex` had the same problem.

Now we keep `:is(…)` when its single child is a selector list. `:is(.foo)` → `.foo` and `:is(*:hover)` → `:hover` still unwrap.

With this fix, `[&:is(.foo,.bar)]:flex` canonicalizes to `[.foo,.bar]:flex`. Both emit `&:is(.foo, .bar)`.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`. It fails without the fix (`expected [ 'foo-or-bar:flex' ] to deeply equal [ '[.foo,.bar]:flex' ]`).
- `vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss` passes.
- `pnpm run build` and `pnpm changelog check` pass.

Issues.Title: Reject duplicate or misordered empty layer and supports clauses in @import
Issues.Body:
Check `layer !== null` and `supports !== null` instead of truthiness in `parseImportParams` so an earlier empty `layer`, `layer()`, or `supports()` clause is still treated as present.

Previously:
- `@import 'a.css' layer layer(utilities)` or `@import 'a.css' layer() layer(utilities)` set `layer = ''`, which failed `if (layer)` on the second `layer` clause and overwrote it instead of returning `null`.

Issues.Title: Skip external imports with mixed-case URI schemes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Keep `@import` URLs with uppercase or mixed-case `http:`, `https:` and `data:` schemes out of the local stylesheet resolver. For example, `@import "HTTPS://example.com/style.css";` currently calls `loadStylesheet()` and can fail the build instead of remaining an external import.

Match these scheme prefixes case-insensitively while preserving the original URL. Add six regressions and a local-file control to ensure filenames such as `./HTTP-Styles.css` keep their casing during resolution.

## Test plan

- All six scheme regressions fail before the fix; the local-file control passes.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project tailwindcss --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=20000`: 5,496 passing, one skipped. The initial default-timeout run passed 5,495 tests and timed out on the existing variant permutation test; the bounded-worker rerun passed it.
- `pnpm --filter tailwindcss build`: passing, including declarations.
- Changed-file Prettier checks, a scoped TypeScript check for the changed source/tests and their imports, and `pnpm changelog check`: passing.
- The package's broad TypeScript task traverses other workspaces and fails with missing modules under this filtered dependency installation. Rust and browser/integration suites were not run for this TypeScript import-handling change.

Issues.Title: Match math function names only at the start of a function name
Issues.Body:
This PR makes sure that a CSS custom function whose name ends in a math function name is not treated as a math function.

`hasMathFn` used a substring match (`input.includes('calc(')`). So `--my-calc(…)` and `--item-rem(…)` counted as math functions, and the value was inferred as a number, percentage, ratio or length:

```
text-[--my-calc(1px)]   → font-size: --my-calc(1px)   (now: color)
text-[--item-rem(1px)]  → font-size: --item-rem(1px)  (now: color)
bg-[--my-calc(1px)]     → background-position: …      (now: background-color)
```

With `abs` and `sign` in `MATH_FUNCTIONS` (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20716), `text-[--design(1px)]` would hit the same bug.

`addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` had the same issue. Its backward scan for the function name stops at `-`, so `w-[--my-calc(1px-2px)]` became `width: --my-calc(1px - 2px)`.

## Changes

- `hasMathFn` scans back from each `(` to the start of the identifier (`a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, `-`, `_`, non-ASCII), and checks that the whole name is a math function. It's also about 4x faster than the 19 `includes` calls in a micro-benchmark on typical values.
- `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` skips a math function name that follows an identifier character, or that is part of a dashed identifier (`--…`). A single `-` before the name still counts as an operator or a sign, so `calc(1px-min(2px,3px))` still becomes `calc(1px - min(2px, 3px))`. The early bail is unchanged.
- Both compare the whole name in lowercase, because CSS function names are case-insensitive. So `Calc(1rem+min(1rem,2rem))` is a length and gets spaces, and `Asin(0.5+0.2)` keeps the spaces it got on `main`. The early bail of the formatter still looks for lowercase names, so an input like `CALC(1px+2px)` is inferred as a length but is not formatted, as on `main`.

Two cases change on purpose. `text-[CALC(1px)]` is now a `font-size` instead of a `color`. And `text-[-min(1px,2px)]` is now a `color` instead of a `font-size`. In CSS, `-min(` is a function named `-min`, not a negated `min(…)`. The formatter still adds the spaces in it.

## Test plan

- Added a `text` test: `calc(…)`, `min(…)` and `calc(min(…))` are still a `font-size`. `--foo(…)`, `--my-calc(…)` and `--item-rem(…)` are a `color`.
- Added formatter cases to `decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts`, including `calc(1px-min(2px,3px))`, `calc(1px*-min(2px,3px))`, `--my-calc(1px-2px)`, `--my-calc(calc(1px-2px))`, `Asin(0.5+0.2)` and `Calc(1px+min(2px,3px))`.
- The new tests fail without the fix.
- `pnpm vitest run --project tailwindcss` passes.
- I compared the output of 1120 candidates on `main` and on this branch: every arbitrary-value candidate with a `(` from `utilities.test.ts` and `variants.test.ts`, plus edge cases in 22 utilities. Only the edge cases with custom functions, names like `fooXcalc(…)`, `écalc(…)`, `\_calc(…)` and `-min(…)`, and mixed-case names like `Calc(…)` and `CALC(…)` changed. No candidate from the test files changed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Match math function names only at the start of a function name" (#20727)

Issues.Title: Remove invalid `justify-baseline` utility
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR removes the invalid `justify-baseline` utility.

Per the [W3C CSS Box Alignment Module Level 3 specification](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-content) and [w3c/csswg-drafts#1184](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1184#issuecomment-295144365), `baseline` is not a valid value for `justify-content` because baseline alignment is only applicable along the cross axis (such as `align-content`, `align-items`), not the main/inline axis. As a result, browsers reject `justify-content: baseline` as invalid syntax.

Fixes #20717

## Test plan

- Ran unit and IntelliSense tests with Vitest:
  ```sh
  pnpm --filter tailwindcss exec vitest run src/intellisense.test.ts src/utilities.test.ts
  ```
  All 422 tests pass.
- Verified code formatting with Prettier.
- Validated changelog fragment with `node ./scripts/changelog.mjs check`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Remove invalid `justify-baseline` utility" (#20721)

Issues.Title: Keep the Changed changelog section for changes that users may have to act on
Issues.Body:
This PR keeps `### Changed` in the changelog for changes that users may have to act on, and documents which section to use.

`[Unreleased]` had a `### Changed` section with two performance entries (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680 and https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20688). A performance improvement is not a change that users have to act on, and the repo already lists them under `### Fixed` (e.g. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20694, https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20678 and https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20663).

## Changes

- `CHANGELOG.md`: remove the `### Changed` section of `[Unreleased]`. Combine the two entries into one entry in `### Fixed`, because https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20688 only extends https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680 to the other integrations. The entry goes in the merge order of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20680.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: move the canonicalization entry of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20697 from `### Added` to `### Fixed`, in merge order, and drop the empty `### Added` heading. A canonicalization improvement is not a new feature for users, and the canonicalization entries of 4.3.4 and 4.3.5 are in `### Fixed` too.
- `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`: add a guide on which section to pick. The examples for `### Changed` come from earlier releases: changes to the CSS of existing utilities, renamed or replaced utilities (also when the upgrade tool migrates them), theme defaults, APIs, stricter parsing, source detection defaults, and supported versions.
- `.changelog/README.md`: link to that guide.

This PR edits `CHANGELOG.md` directly instead of adding a fragment, because it fixes entries that the "Compile changelog" workflow already compiled. Released sections stay as they are. The PR changes only docs, so it needs no changelog entry of its own.

## Test plan

- `pnpm changelog check` passes.
- `pnpm --silent changelog` shows `[Unreleased]` with only `### Fixed`.
- `pnpm prettier --check` passes for the three files.

Issues.Title: Use napi's module retain helper to keep Oxide loaded [ci-all]
Issues.Body:
This PR replaces the Windows-only `GetModuleHandleExW` FFI from https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20471 with the helper that napi-rs now ships for the same purpose: `napi::bindgen_prelude::retain_current_module_for_unload_safety()` (added in https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/pull/3423, released in 3.12.1).

The `#[napi(module_exports)]` hook now calls the helper once. That keeps the Oxide addon mapped after a Node worker that loaded it exits, so Rayon threads that outlive the worker don't crash with `0xC0000005` (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20470).

Changes:

- Bump `napi` from 3.11.0 to 3.16.2 and `napi-derive` from 3.6.0 to 3.7.1.
- Remove our own `unsafe` FFI block.

Behavior changes compared to https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20471:

- The helper is best effort. If pinning fails, `require` no longer throws. The addon then behaves as it did before the pin existed.
- The helper also pins the module on Linux and macOS (`dladdr` + `dlopen(RTLD_NOLOAD)`), not only on Windows.
- The helper does not exist on wasm, so the hook is `#[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]`. The wasm build had no pin before either.

This is an internal change with no new effect for users, so it has no changelog fragment.

## Test plan

- `pnpm run build` (includes the wasm build)
- `cargo test -p tailwind-oxide`
- `env -u NODE_ENV pnpm vitest run --root=integrations oxide/workers`
- `[ci-all]` in the title so CI runs `integrations/oxide/workers.test.ts` on Windows and macOS too.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Use napi's module retain helper to keep Oxide loaded [ci-all]" (#20726)

Issues.Title: `@apply` of a CSS mixin with a space in its arguments gives the error "both mixins and utilities"
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`@apply` of a CSS mixin with a space in its arguments gives the error "both mixins and utilities"" (#20724)

Issues.Title: Allow spaces in the arguments of a CSS mixin in `@apply`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@apply` with a CSS mixin threw "You cannot use `@apply` with both mixins and utilities" as soon as the mixin arguments had a space, e.g. `@apply --card(red, 2rem)`. The params were split on every whitespace, so `--card(red,` was seen as a mixin and `2rem)` as a utility.

The params are now split with `segment`, so whitespace inside parens, brackets, braces and strings is kept in the same part. The dependency scan and the circular dependency check use the same split, so a mixin argument like `card` in `@utility card { @apply --card({ red, card }, 2rem); }` is not read as a utility. A list of valid utilities splits the same way as before.

Fixes #20724

## Test plan

- Added `@apply --my-mixin-1(red, 2rem)` and `@apply --my-mixin-1({ 1px, 2px }, 3px)` to the existing "should be usable with CSS mixins" test in `index.test.ts`. It fails without this change and passes with it.
- Added a test with `@apply --card({ red, card }, 2rem)` inside `@utility card`. It fails with a circular dependency error without this change.
- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: all tests pass.
- `pnpm changelog check` passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Allow spaces in the arguments of a CSS mixin in `@apply`" (#20725)

Issues.Title: Optimize `@tailwindcss/webpack` output in webpack production mode
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Building with `webpack --mode production` (or `mode: 'production'` in the config) ships unminified CSS from `@tailwindcss/webpack`, even though the README says `optimize` defaults to `true` in production mode. The loader only checks `process.env.NODE_ENV`, and webpack's mode doesn't set that in the Node process (webpack-cli only does with `--node-env`). The loader now also checks `this.mode === 'production'`.

## Test plan

Added an integration test that runs `pnpm webpack --mode=production` and expects minified CSS. Also checked by hand against the published 4.3.5 loader in a scratch project: unminified before the change, minified after, and development mode stays unminified.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Optimize `@tailwindcss/webpack` output in webpack production mode" (#20723)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: keep arbitrary variants a compound variant can't replace
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Canonicalization rewrites `not-[&>*]:flex` to `not-*:flex` (and `not-[&_*]:flex` to `not-**:flex`). `*` and `**` can't be used inside `not-*`, so the new class generates no CSS at all.

`arbitraryVariants` walks into compound variants and swaps the inner variant for one with the same signature, without checking that the compound variant accepts it. This skips the replacement when the parent compound variant doesn't compound with the replacement, using the same `compoundsWith` check the candidate parser uses.

## Test plan

- Added `not-[&>*]:flex` and `not-[&_*]:flex` to the arbitrary variant tests in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`, expecting them to stay as-is. On `main` they fail (`not-*:flex`, `not-**:flex`), with the fix they pass.
- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: all tests pass.
- `prettier --check` and `pnpm changelog check` pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Canonicalization: keep arbitrary variants a compound variant can't replace" (#20720)
